definition: Independent alternative international links, gateways or landing facilities that maintain connectivity after failure. Additional international capacity alone is insufficient.
Physically independent domestic paths, rings or loops that preserve connectivity after failure. Critical-site links may also qualify when explicit.
An alternative communications link using a different technology to maintain connectivity after primary-link failure.
Multiple providers explicitly used to maintain service after a provider failure. Provider plurality alone is insufficient.
Independent alternative communications links to a critical facility. Route, technology or provider types may also qualify when explicit.
Duplicate network nodes, operations centres or exchanges that preserve communications after failure. Generic duplication without a continuity function is insufficient.
